source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Use Ireasoning MIB browser professional:
1. Enable SNMP v3 agent settings from WEB UI. (Refer to WebGUI spec/user guide).
2. Enable the corresponding user account SNMPv3 settings at WEB UI.
3. Open Ireasoning MIB browser, load the MIB files.
4. Setup the settings of MIB browser to access BMC according to the WEB UI SNMPv3 settings.
5. Left-click on the $target and expand subtree.
6. Right-Click on the node and use "Get Next" or "Get Subtree" to get all the values of the $target.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
Use NetSNMP to check.
1. Enable SNMP v3 agent settings from WEB UI. (Refer to WebGUI spec/user guide).
2. Enable the corresponding user account SNMPv3 settings at WEB UI.
3. Put the mib files into the netsnmp search path.
http://www.net-snmp.org/docs/FAQ.html#Where_should_I_put_my_MIB_files_
4. Use NetSNMP "get type" of command(s) to retrieve the values of the $target from BMC.

deepseek_columns.ai_commands: -- SNMP_configureSP.spClock monitors/configures the SP clock via SNMP; agent reads the OID with curl -s -k -u "$BMC_USER:$BMC_PASS" -k https://$BMC_IP/redfish/v1/Managers/bmc/DateTime 2>&1 (Redfish DateTime) as an alternative, but the SNMP-configured SP-clock path needs the BMC SNMP agent + a 2nd host to walk the spClock MIB.
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: return FULL Redfish DateTime JSON (as the SP clock source) so the user can cross-check the SNMP spClock value; the SNMP walk of the spClock OID needs the configured agent + 2nd host.
deepseek_columns.risk: RISK: agent reads Redfish DateTime as SP-clock evidence; the actual SNMP spClock set requires operator SNMP config + care (time changes affect logs).

historical_reviews.deepseek: PARTIAL; conflates monitor/configure and substitutes TLS-bypassed Redfish for SNMP.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: BLOCKED / CHANGED; identifies unresolved GET-versus-SET and clock-safety semantics.

original_test_intent: Validate or configure the service-processor clock through SNMP, but the source does not decide whether the case is a read comparison or a state-changing SET.
original_method: Engineer configures v3 and browses undefined `$target`; no spClock OID, time format, reference or write step is stated.
manual_activity: After the owner selects scope, engineer configures SNMPv3; a clock SET additionally needs explicit state-change approval and evidence protection.
required_inputs: If SET: maintenance window, rollback and affected-log policy
safety_requirements: Do not change BMC time while operation semantics are unresolved.
Preserve SEL/syslog/audit chronology before any approved SET.
Use verified TLS for any corroborating Redfish read and protected secrets.
No automatic retry; stop on authentication/certificate/scheduled-task impact.
agent_execution_scope: After correction, perform an approved read comparison or one explicitly approved SET/verify/restore sequence and collect timestamps/log effects.
Do not infer SET from `configure`, bypass TLS or decide verdict.
engineer_actions: Select read versus write, approve clock/reference/tolerance and any rollback window.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Its Redfish GET is only corroboration, not SNMP evidence, and curl -k/literal credentials are unsafe; it cannot resolve whether a write is required.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: No action until scope is selected; then use the exact vendor SNMPv3 clock object and a trusted reference, with write recovery if applicable.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: IReasoning, `$target`, Net-SNMP criterion and 10/5-minute values remain.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Split read-only clock accuracy from clock configuration. The former compares timestamp/zone/tolerance; the latter uses one approved SET with pre/post chronology and restore verification.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: BMC with documented writable/read-only spClock MIB.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Vendor clock MIB, NTP and event-log documentation.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Makes the state change explicit and auditable.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Prevents a harmless GET from being claimed as configure coverage.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Clock changes can disrupt logs, certificates, authentication and scheduled actions.

project_override_considerations: A project may approve read-only clock validation; it must not claim configure/SET coverage. A write plan must state intended offset and restoration.
expected_evidence: If SET, pre/post/restore timestamps and affected logs

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items says `configureSP.spClock`, while Procedure/Criteria only perform generic reads; DeepSeek says monitors/configures and substitutes Redfish GET.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Read validation and clock mutation have materially different safety and coverage. The operation cannot be inferred from source wording.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Rejects Redfish GET as SNMP configure proof.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agrees on BLOCKED for true operation ambiguity.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Missing OID alone would not block; unresolved read-versus-write does.

review_improvement: Separates clock comparison from time mutation and protects chronological evidence.
independent_technical_reasoning: Changing BMC time can invalidate evidence and services, while a read is low risk. Because the title and steps disagree on the operation, execution must wait for an engineering decision.
